title: The Peppered Moth
principle: This really happened, and people wrote the numbers down.

t: Somebody actually counted. Every year, for a hundred years, in real woods.
The beetles were a simulation. This one is not: people counted real moths, in real woods, every year, for over a century — and the counts are still being taken.
sub: So we can check whether any of this is true.
This is the lesson where the mechanism stops being a model and becomes a measurement.

question: Britain's trees got covered in soot from factories. What happened to the pale moths?
Industrial soot darkened the tree trunks the moths rested on. Predict the consequence for the pale form.
options: They became easier for birds to see, and got rarer
Nothing — moths are too small to matter
stages.outcome: They became easier for birds to see, and got rarer
note: Guess first. You already know the mechanism.
Commit. The second option is the Lamarckian answer, and separating it from the first is the whole point of the last two lessons.

t: Start with pale ground, like clean bark. Get the moths matching. Then darken the ground, the way soot did.
Run it on a pale background first, then darken it partway through — that is the industrial revolution, at speed.
goal: The population followed the ground. That is exactly what the real moths did.
The population tracked the background. In the real woods it took about fifty years, and it was counted the whole way.

t: The switches are back. Then the Clean Air Acts happened and the bark got pale again — try running it backwards.
Conditions exposed again. After the Clean Air Acts the trunks lightened and the dark form declined just as fast. Reproduce that reversal, and satisfy yourself it needs no new mechanism.
goal: It goes both ways, with the same three conditions. Nothing new was needed.
The reversal required no additional mechanism — only the background changing back. A theory that predicts the return trip as well as the outward one is doing real work.

t: This really happened, and people wrote the numbers down.
Industrial melanism in the peppered moth, Biston betularia. Measured, published, argued over, re-measured, and confirmed.
The dark form went from under 2% to over 90% in polluted areas in about fifty years, then reversed after clean-air legislation. Both directions were tracked by direct counting.

Kettlewell's original 1950s experiments were later criticised on methodology — moths pinned to trunks, releases in unnatural densities — and creationist critiques made much of that. Michael Majerus then spent seven years, 2001 to 2007, redoing it properly with natural resting positions, and the result held. That sequence is worth as much as the finding: a challenged result was re-tested and survived.
sub: The moths did not change. Which moths survived did.
No moth ever changed colour. Both forms existed the whole time, in different proportions.
The dark form is a single dominant allele that was present before the soot and rare, exactly as the mechanism requires.

That last point is the load-bearing one: the variation preceded the environmental change. Had the dark form appeared only after the trunks darkened, this would be evidence for something else entirely.

q: Did the moths change colour when the trees got sooty?
Did individual moths darken in response to the soot?
Why is the pre-existence of the dark allele critical to the interpretation?
options: No — the dark ones were always there and simply did better
why: Both kinds of moth were around before the soot. The dark ones were rare because they stood out. Once the bark went dark, they were the ones that were hard to see.
No individual changed. The dark form existed at low frequency beforehand and simply became the one the birds missed. The population's composition changed and not one moth did.

Because it distinguishes selection from a directed response to the environment. Variation arising before the pressure is the signature of selection; variation arising in response to it would be Lamarckian, and that is precisely what Luria and Delbrück ruled out for bacteria in 1943.

t: The moths came back pale after the air got cleaner. That is a prediction that came true.

The strongest thing about this case is not the original change but the reversal. The mechanism predicted that cleaning the air would run it backwards, legislation cleaned the air, and it did — on the predicted timescale. An explanation that only accounts for what already happened is cheap; one that forecasts the return trip is not.
